hypotheses.reasoning: notif-worker crash-loops on one message, msg-223156 at offset 479309 of notifications.outbound. Each restart resumes at the same committed offset (#111, #118, #127) and fails identically with RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded in expandReferences (#107, #112, #120). The consumer never commits past the bad message, so the restarts repeat and the lag grows. Earlier batches processed fine (#106, lag 40ms), so the failure is specific to this payload. The broker lag warnings (#125, #158, #187, #204) are downstream effects of the stalled consumer. Upstream services show no errors (notification-svc, template-svc, redis, notif-db all 0 error+). Alternative: a bad_deploy of v4.19.7 introduced unbounded recursion in expandReferences (version string at #109). The trigger is a single message, so the poison-message reading fits better.

If expandReferences recursion is a regression in v4.19.7, any payload with deep references would crash the worker, not just this one. Only one message has been observed failing, so this is less likely, but it is the alternative if other payloads also fail.

verdict.recommendedAction: Skip or dead-letter offset 479309 (msg-223156) so the consumer can advance, then restart notif-worker. Inspect the msg-223156 payload for a self-referencing or deeply nested reference chain, and fix or quarantine the producer that emitted it. Add a recursion depth guard in expandReferences. If other payloads also crash the worker, roll notif-worker back from v4.19.7 to the previous release.
